a153a37894cc:
"The Saint of the Prisons" Valeriu Gafencu and the Holy Brâncoveanu Martyrs – icon painted on glass –

18 February 2022 marks 70 years since the falling asleep in the Lord of the young Valeriu Gafencu (a student at the Faculty of Law and Philosophy in Iași), one of the young Romanian intellectuals who lit up and sanctified the communist prisons with their lives. In these prisons they were tortured, humiliated and subjected to unimaginable torment for many years (at Aiud, for example), or "re-educated" by the murderous torturers of the communist extermination camps (at Pitești). Some of these martyrs miraculously survived and told us about the horrors they endured; otherwise we would never have known the whole truth. Valeriu Gafencu, however [born in Sângerei (Bălți County, in Bessarabia) on 24 January 1921], died in Târgu Ocna prison at the age of 31.

Valeriu Gafencu – the Saint of the Prisons:
"Seek happiness in your souls. Do not seek it outside yourselves. Do not expect happiness to come from anywhere other than from within you, from your soul, where the Lord of Love, Christ, dwells. If you expect happiness from outside yourselves, you will suffer disappointment after disappointment and will never reach it."

• Tomorrow we celebrate Saint George the Great Martyr, the Victory-bearer, called “the spiritual springtime”.

• Two of the works painted in our workshop depicting Saint George the Great Martyr are these icons painted on glass, which we are showing you today (model: Arpașu de Sus, early 19th century).

• About the icon
The scene shows the soldier saint George, born in Beirut; he was an army commander under Diocletian, defended the Christians and was martyred in 303 AD, and he is one of the most venerated saints.
He rides a white horse, dressed in armour and a cloak, with a lance that has a cross at one end, and under the horse is the dragon pierced by the lance. Behind the saint, on the horse's rump, sits the boy Leo of Amira with a jug in his hand, which he was taking to his master in the field when Saint George freed him from slavery to the Bulgars. In the distance are the emperor's daughter, saved from the dragon's claws, and the emperor throwing him the keys of the city. (Wikipedia)

• Happy name day to the friends and followers of our page whose names come from Saint George!🥀

e734dcf67935:
⚜️Saint Charalambos the Hieromartyr (10 February)⚜️
• On 10 February the Romanian Orthodox Church celebrates Saint Charalambos, protector of the poor and the sick and deliverer from plague, a saint to whom the Romanian peasant (especially in 18th–19th century Transylvania) once prayed for protection from plague, cholera, typhoid fever and the other epidemics that used to ravage people. The same Romanian peasant “painted” Saint Charalambos in countless icons on glass. One of them (painted in Șcheii Brașovului in the 19th century) is the model of the icon I am showing you today, an icon painted in our workshop (in the traditional technique) three years ago
• About the icon: the icon shows Saint Charalambos binding the plague, and so saving the city. Charalambos is shown in the usual way (standing, dressed in robe, mantle and omophorion, with the holy book and halo, giving a blessing), trampling the plague, which is bound by a chain fastened to his belt. The plague, carrying a scythe, has the face of a horned man. On either side of the saint, in the background, the image is enriched by a cityscape with palaces and fortified walls. The ground is rendered by bands of colour bearing hatching, crosses and flowers. From high in the sky the scene is watched over by Jesus, who blesses him, and by an angel holding out a wreath of flowers to him. They are seated on clouds. On the light-blue background are large unoutlined flowers and yellow, white and black stars (source of the description: the National Museum of Art of Romania)
4befd41bb25f:
~Saint Charalambos – icon painted on glass (model: Șcheii Brașovului)~
On 10 February the Romanian Orthodox Church celebrates Saint Charalambos, a saint to whom the Romanian peasant once prayed for protection from plague, cholera, typhoid fever and the other epidemics that used to ravage people. That is why there are many icons on glass in which the Romanian peasant of 18th-century Transylvania painted the face of Saint Charalambos, the deliverer from disease, and also from famine.
The icon is not available. I will paint it again to order.

About the icon (source: the National Museum of Art of Romania)
 The icon shows Saint Charalambos binding the plague, and so saving the city. Charalambos is shown in the usual way (standing, dressed in robe, mantle and omophorion, with the holy book and halo, giving a blessing): he tramples the plague, which is bound by a chain fastened to his belt. The plague, carrying a scythe, has the face of a horned man. On either side of the saint, in the background, the image is enriched by a cityscape with palaces and fortified walls. The ground is rendered by bands of colour bearing hatching, crosses, flowers and dots. From high in the sky the scene is watched over by Jesus, who blesses him, and by an angel holding out a wreath of flowers to him. They are seated on clouds. On the light-blue background are large unoutlined flowers and yellow, white and black stars. Colours: light blue, white, brown, coral red, black, ochre, gold.
